purpose: Distinguish (A) model generalisation failure from (B) custom-extractor mismatch.
extractor_note: Python cicflowmeter port (hieulw), NOT the Java CICFlowMeter V3 the CIC-IDS2018 authors used. Explicit, documented substitution.

definition_notes.units: Flow Duration and all IAT features are MICROSECONDS in both the CIC dataset and this cicflowmeter port (verified: an ~18 s real flow reads ~18.7e6). No unit conversion is applied.
definition_notes.Fwd Pkt Len / TotLen: The port's packet-length features include L3/L4 header bytes, whereas the Live extractor and CIC use the L4 payload. This is a real definition difference (reported), not corrected here.
definition_notes.flow_segmentation: The port cuts flows on an activity/idle timeout and does not create the short post-FIN residual flows the Live engine does, so the flow COUNT per capture differs.
definition_notes.Fwd Seg Size Min / Init Fwd Win Byts: Both agree with the Live extractor (20 and 8192 for real FTP) and both differ from CIC (40 and 26883) — the SHAP-critical features are NOT moved toward CIC by switching extractor.

section_11_verdict.headline: CICFlowMeter FTP recall 0.000 vs custom 0.000 (+0.000) — NOT a substantial improvement: switching to an independent CICFlowMeter does not recover FTP detection, so the failure is MODEL GENERALISATION (A), not our custom extractor. No retraining is performed in this experiment.

limitation: Only 5 real PCAPs (42 custom / 22 cicflowmeter flows); Python port, not Java V3.
